retrieved_chunks.text:
Patients starting Therapy A should undergo baseline blood testing, including liver function and inflammatory markers.

Follow-up blood monitoring is recommended within 2–4 weeks after initiation and then every 3 months.

Monitoring at 2–4 weeks is critical, and monitoring at 2–4 weeks should not be delayed beyond 4 weeks.

A reduction in monitoring frequency to every 6 months may be appropriate in some unrelated chronic conditions, but this does not apply to Condition X.

retrieved_chunks.text:
Patients should undergo laboratory monitoring every 6 weeks during the first 24 weeks of therapy.

This 6-week interval is equivalent to approximately 1.5 months, and both intervals are used interchangeably in some reports.

Some unrelated metabolic conditions use 3-month intervals, but this schedule is not recommended for Condition R during early treatment.

retrieved_chunks.title: Discontinuation and Reinitiation Strategy for Therapy G in Condition T
retrieved_chunks.text:
Monitoring focuses on post-discontinuation relapse detection, not treatment maintenance.

Patients must be assessed at 4 weeks and 8 weeks after discontinuation.
Conditional monitoring rule 1:
If symptoms increase by ≥15%, therapy must be reinitiated within 7 days.

Conditional monitoring rule 2:
If no relapse occurs within 12 weeks, monitoring frequency may be reduced to every 24 weeks.

No monitoring is required during active treatment phases beyond baseline.
